subject.name: Math
subject.title: Fractions, decimals and shapes
subject.description: 8 aulas • laboratórios de toque, frações, decimais, problemas, perímetro e área.

lessons.title: Fractions of a whole
lessons.subtitle: Numerator, denominator and equal parts
lessons.intro: A fraction represents equal parts of a whole. The denominator tells how many equal parts make one whole; the numerator tells how many of those parts are selected.

facts.text: The pieces must have the same size. Four unequal pieces do not make fourths.
In 3/4, 3 is the numerator: three parts are selected.
In 3/4, 4 is the denominator: one whole is split into four equal parts.
1/2 = one half; 1/3 = one third; 1/4 = one fourth; 1/5 = one fifth; 1/6 = one sixth; 1/7 = one seventh; 1/8 = one eighth.
All the parts together make one whole: 4/4 = 1 and 6/6 = 1.

lessons.remember: Denominator = equal parts in ONE whole. Numerator = parts selected.

lessons.title: Fraction of a set
lessons.subtitle: Share equally, then choose groups
lessons.intro: To find a fraction of a set, divide the total into the number of equal groups shown by the denominator. Then take the number of groups shown by the numerator.

facts.text: 1/5 of 20 marbles: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 marbles.
3/4 of 56 students: 56 ÷ 4 × 3 = 42 students.
1/4 of 56 students = 14 students.
24 cupcakes shared equally by 6 teachers: 24 ÷ 6 = 4 cupcakes each.

facts.term: Do not mix up the total
facts.text: When finding 1/5 of 20, the denominator is 5. The total number of objects is 20.

lessons.remember: Total ÷ denominator × numerator. Keep the unit in your answer.

lessons.title: Equivalent fractions and mixed numbers
lessons.subtitle: Same value, different parts
lessons.intro: Equivalent fractions represent the same amount of the same whole. A mixed number combines a whole-number part and a fraction.

facts.text: Multiply or divide BOTH numerator and denominator by the same nonzero number: 2/5 = 4/10; 12/24 = 6/12.
The numerator is smaller than the denominator: 2/5 is less than one.
The numerator is at least the denominator. 7/3 is greater than one; 3/3 is exactly one.
Whole × denominator + numerator gives the new numerator. Keep the denominator: 2 1/3 = 7/3.
Divide numerator by denominator: 7 ÷ 3 = 2 remainder 1, so 7/3 = 2 1/3.

lessons.remember: Equal value needs the SAME whole. Change numerator and denominator together.

lessons.title: Tenths and hundredths
lessons.subtitle: Fractions, grids and decimal numbers
lessons.intro: A decimal point separates the whole-number part from the decimal part. The first place after the point is tenths; the second is hundredths.

facts.text: 1.2 = one and two tenths. 71.82 = seventy-one and eighty-two hundredths. You can also read digits after “point”.
35/100 = 0.35; 5/100 = 0.05. The zero in the tenths place matters.
Compare wholes, then tenths, then hundredths. 0.89 < 0.90. Increasing order: 0.09, 0.89, 0.9, 1.4, 1.45, 2.65, 4.09.

lessons.remember: 0.6 = 0.60, but 0.06 is different. One whole grid contains 100 hundredths.

lessons.title: Adding and subtracting decimals
lessons.subtitle: Line up the decimal points
lessons.intro: Write the numbers in columns with decimal points directly under each other. Add or subtract from right to left, regrouping when needed.

facts.text: Ones under ones, tenths under tenths, hundredths under hundredths.
3.2 = 3.20. A final zero helps line up places without changing the value.
76.3 − 34.1 = 42.2. For 3.20 − 2.85, regroup: the result is 0.35.
Write the answer’s decimal point directly under the points above.

lessons.remember: Line up the POINTS, not the last digits. Check each column.

lessons.title: Money, distance and temperature
lessons.subtitle: Choose the operation and explain
lessons.intro: Read what the question asks before choosing an operation. Keep money, distance and temperature units in the answer.

facts.text: Saved i$260; i$5 left means spending i$255. Check how many activities the question asks for.
Free play 25; movie 200; movie with popcorn 140; digital center 60; all centers 100; free clothing 150; buddy reading 30, all in i$.
Free play + movie with popcorn + digital center + buddy reading: 25 + 140 + 60 + 30 = 255; 260 − 255 = 5.
Liam ran 3.2 km; Jack ran 2.85 km. “How much farther?” means subtract: 3.20 − 2.85 = 0.35 km.
From Salvador: Belo Horizonte 1,370 km; Brasília 1,460; Rio de Janeiro 1,640; São Paulo 1,960; Curitiba 2,100, in increasing order.

lessons.remember: Read → choose an operation → calculate → check the unit and the question.

lessons.title: Perimeter
lessons.subtitle: Walk around the outside
lessons.intro: Perimeter is the total distance around the outside of a flat shape. Add all the side lengths, using the same unit.

facts.text: Opposite sides are equal. With length 5 m and width 3 m: 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16 m.
Four equal sides. A square with side 25 cm has perimeter 100 cm.
All sides are equal. To find one side, divide the perimeter by the number of sides.
Square: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm. Regular pentagon: 25 ÷ 5 = 5 cm. Regular hexagon: 60 ÷ 6 = 10 cm.
500 m = 0.5 km. A square with 500 m sides has perimeter 2 km; a triangle with three 1 km sides has 3 km; a 1.2 km × 0.5 km rectangle has 3.4 km.
Do not assume two triangle sides are equal just because they look equal. You need lengths, equality marks or a statement.

lessons.remember: Perimeter = outside boundary. Use cm, m or km, without a square sign.

lessons.title: Area and a house on a grid
lessons.subtitle: Count square units inside
lessons.intro: Area measures the space inside a shape. Count the square units that cover it. For a rectangle or square, multiply length by width.

facts.text: One 1 cm × 1 cm square has area 1 cm². Area units include cm² and m².
A 9 m × 6 m rectangle has area 9 × 6 = 54 m² and perimeter 30 m.
A 5 × 5 square covers 25 square units.
A 4 × 3 grid has 12 square units. A 5 × 6 grid has 30. A 3 × 3 grid has 9.
First bedroom: 8 cm² blue; second bedroom: 6 cm² yellow; bathroom: 4 cm² red; kitchen: 12 cm² green; living room: 16 cm² orange; balcony: 2 cm² pink.
The same area can have different perimeters. A 2 × 6 rectangle and a 3 × 4 rectangle both cover 12 square units, but their perimeters are 16 and 14 units.

lessons.remember: Area = inside squares. Perimeter = outside edges. Label each with the right unit.

m3-fractions.title: Numerator, denominator and equal parts
paragraphs: For the same whole, a larger denominator means smaller pieces. One sixth is smaller than one fourth, because the whole was divided into more pieces.
Português: denominador indica em quantas partes iguais o inteiro foi dividido; numerador conta as partes escolhidas.
vocabulary: denominador: partes iguais em um inteiro
m3-fractions.example: Divide one circle into 6 equal parts. Select 4: the fraction is 4/6.
m3-fractions.challenge: Draw a whole divided into 8 equal parts and shade 3. Label the numerator and denominator.

m3-sets.title: Share equally, then choose groups
paragraphs: A set is a collection of objects. The denominator tells how many equal groups to form; it is not automatically the number of objects.
Português: primeiro divida pelo número de grupos; depois pegue a quantidade de grupos pedida.
vocabulary: de: encontrar a parte da quantidade
m3-sets.example: 3/4 of 56: four groups of 14; select three groups, so 14 + 14 + 14 = 42.
m3-sets.challenge: There are 24 counters. Find 1/6 and 5/6 of the set. Show the equal groups.

m3-equivalence.title: Same value, different parts
paragraphs: Examples in the school material: 1 2/6 = 8/6; 2 2/3 = 8/3; 2 5/6 = 17/6; 1 3/8 = 11/8. Count all selected parts across the wholes.
Português: número misto tem inteiro e fração. Para transformar, conte quantas partes cabem nos inteiros e acrescente as restantes.
m3-equivalence.example: 2 5/6: two wholes contain 12 sixths; add 5 sixths: 17/6.
m3-equivalence.challenge: Show that 1/2 = 3/6. Then convert 2 1/3 to an improper fraction.

m3-decimals.title: Fractions, grids and decimal numbers
paragraphs: Each square in a 10 × 10 chart is one hundredth; each complete row of ten squares is one tenth. Ten tenths and one hundred hundredths both make one whole.
The material uses both decimal points and decimal commas. In the games, 1.06 and 1,06 are accepted as the same value. Commas in the distance table, such as 1,960 km, separate thousands.
m3-decimals.example: Shade 47 of 100 cells: 47/100 = 0.47. Shade a whole grid and 6 more cells: 1.06.
m3-decimals.challenge: Write 0.8 and 0.09 as fractions. Put 1.4, 0.89 and 0.9 in increasing order.

m3-operations.title: Line up the decimal points
paragraphs: If a column adds to ten or more, carry to the next place. In subtraction, exchange one unit for ten tenths or one tenth for ten hundredths when needed.
Português: alinhe os separadores, complete com zeros e faça a conta da direita para a esquerda.
m3-operations.example: 3.20 − 2.85: exchange one tenth for ten hundredths, then one unit for ten tenths. Result: 0.35.
m3-operations.challenge: Set out and solve 22.3 + 34.1 and 3.2 − 2.85 in columns.

m3-problems.title: Choose the operation and explain
paragraphs: “Left as change” asks how much remains after spending. “Farther than” compares two distances. “Rise by” tells how much to add.
Português: procure o que está sendo pedido; não escolha a operação só porque viu uma palavra. Confira o sentido da resposta no problema.
m3-problems.example: A budget of 260 with 5 left allows a total cost of 255. Select exactly four activities and check both conditions.
m3-problems.challenge: Find how much farther Liam ran than Jack and tomorrow’s temperature after a 2.5°C rise from 29.8°C.

m3-perimeter.title: Walk around the outside
paragraphs: Perimeter can also be counted along the exposed edges of square cells. An edge shared by two cells is inside the shape, so do not count it.
Português: contorno é diferente de espaço por dentro. Em polígonos regulares, divida o contorno pelo número de lados para descobrir um lado.
m3-perimeter.challenge: Find the perimeter of a 40 cm × 10 cm rectangle. A regular hexagon has perimeter 60 cm: find one side.

m3-area.title: Count square units inside
paragraphs: For an irregular shape made of full squares, count each square once. In the house, rooms must not overlap and the cells of each room should connect along edges.
Português: área conta os quadradinhos por dentro. No retângulo, linhas × colunas dá a quantidade de quadradinhos.
m3-area.example: A room 11 m long and 7 m wide has area 77 m² and perimeter 36 m.
m3-area.challenge: Draw a room with area 12 square units. Give its length, width, area and perimeter.
